column3: The Hebrew leaves the appearing subject implicit; BSB explicitly names the LORD.
The Hebrew leaves the builder unnamed in this clause; BSB names Solomon.
The Hebrew gives a height of one hundred twenty; BSB gives twenty.
The Hebrew calls this the large house; BSB identifies the main room.
The Hebrew calls the building the house; BSB uses temple.
The Hebrew explicitly names the house before its components; BSB begins with its beams.
The Hebrew does not separately specify inside in the gold covering clause.
The Hebrew calls the upper rooms plural; BSB uses upper area.
The Hebrew uses a plural subject for overlaying the cherubim; BSB uses he.
The Hebrew calls this the one cherub and says the other wing clung to the other cherub’s wing; BSB numbers the cherubim and uses touched.
The Hebrew directs their faces toward the house; BSB specifies the main room.
The Hebrew says he put cherubim on the curtain, without separately stating weaving or yarn.
The Hebrew states thirty-five cubits in length without together or each; BSB describes a combined height and a capital on each pillar.
The Hebrew locates the making of chains in the inner sanctuary; BSB calls them interwoven chains.
The Hebrew uses right and left; BSB interprets them as south and north.
